name: Vancouver
tagline: Rainforest, seawall and snowy peaks on the edge of the Pacific
description:
Vancouver might be the only big city where you can ski in the morning, paddle past seals at lunchtime and eat spot prawns beside a glassy harbor at sunset. The snowy North Shore mountains rise directly behind its forest of glass towers, temperate rainforest creeps to the edge of downtown, and a seawall of nearly 30 kilometers invites you to walk, cycle or skate along the water.

The neighborhoods reflect the city's outward-looking spirit. Cobbled Gastown mixes Victorian brick with cocktail bars, Chinatown hides one of the finest classical Chinese gardens outside China, and Granville Island's public market is a feast for every sense. Across the water, laid-back Kitsilano draws beach volleyball players and yoga devotees, while Commercial Drive keeps its Italian cafés and indie spirit alive.

Indigenous art and culture are central here, from the monumental carvings at the Museum of Anthropology to the totem poles of Stanley Park, a reminder that the city stands on the unceded lands of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations. Food is an adventure too, with some of North America's best dim sum, izakaya and sushi alongside wild salmon and farm-to-table bistros. Pack a rain jacket, but on a clear day few places anywhere look this good.

safety.notes: Vancouver is very safe overall, but the Downtown Eastside around East Hastings Street has visible street disorder and open drug use, so pass through quickly by day or detour around it. Car break-ins are common, so never leave valuables in a parked car.

tipping: Tip 18–20% at restaurants and bars, where card machines prompt you, and about 15% for taxis; sales taxes of 5–12% are added at the register on top of menu prices.
gettingAround: SkyTrain, buses and the SeaBus ferry cover the region, and the Canada Line runs from the airport to downtown in about 25 minutes; just tap a contactless card or Compass card. The seawall and protected bike lanes make cycling the most scenic way to get around.
tips: Rent a bike near Denman Street and ride the Stanley Park seawall counterclockwise, which is the required direction for cyclists, pausing at Prospect Point for the Lions Gate Bridge view.
After 6:30 p.m. on weekdays and all day on weekends, a single-zone fare covers the entire transit network, including the SeaBus to North Vancouver.
Capilano Suspension Bridge and Grouse Mountain run free shuttles from Canada Place in season; if budget matters, the Lynn Canyon suspension bridge is free.
Fit hikers can climb the steep Grouse Grind trail in summer and buy a cheaper one-way ticket to ride the gondola down.
From October to April it rains often, so keep museums, the aquarium and Granville Island's indoor market for wet days.
Spot prawn season in May and June is a local obsession; buy them fresh off the boats at the False Creek fishermen's wharf.
etiquette: Many events open by acknowledging the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations; listen respectfully and ask before photographing Indigenous ceremonies.
Locals often call out 'thank you' to the bus driver when leaving, even by the back door.
Stick to the marked walking and cycling lanes on the seawall, which are separated for a reason.
Canadians apologize reflexively; a quick 'sorry' when brushing past someone is simply polite.

neighborhoods.name: Gastown
neighborhoods.blurb: The city's cobblestoned birthplace, where Victorian warehouses hold cocktail bars, design shops and some of Vancouver's best restaurants.

neighborhoods.name: Kitsilano
neighborhoods.blurb: A breezy beach neighborhood of wooden character homes, yoga studios, brunch cafés and sunset views across English Bay.

neighborhoods.name: Yaletown
neighborhoods.blurb: Former rail warehouses converted into loft apartments, patios and wine bars, stepping down to the False Creek seawall and marina.

neighborhoods.name: Mount Pleasant
neighborhoods.blurb: Vancouver's creative heart along Main Street, packed with craft breweries, vintage shops, murals and independent coffee roasters.

neighborhoods.name: Commercial Drive
neighborhoods.blurb: Known simply as 'the Drive', a multicultural strip of old-school Italian cafés, global eateries and a proudly bohemian crowd.

dishes.name: Wild sockeye salmon
dishes.description: Deep-red Pacific salmon, often grilled on cedar planks, candied with maple or smoked in the Indigenous tradition.

dishes.name: BC spot prawns
dishes.description: Sweet, tender local prawns with a short spring season, best simply cooked in butter and garlic or eaten raw as sashimi.

dishes.name: BC roll
dishes.description: A Vancouver-born sushi roll filled with barbecued salmon skin and cucumber, found on nearly every local sushi menu.

dishes.name: Nanaimo bar
dishes.description: A no-bake British Columbia treat of chocolate-coconut crumb base, custard buttercream and a snappy chocolate top.

dishes.name: Dim sum
dishes.description: Thanks to a large Cantonese community, the city and neighboring Richmond serve some of the finest dumplings, buns and rice rolls outside Asia.

events.name: Polar Bear Swim
events.description: On New Year's Day, thousands of costumed swimmers charge into the icy waters of English Bay in a tradition dating back more than a century.

events.name: Vancouver Cherry Blossom Festival
events.description: Tens of thousands of cherry trees bloom across the city, celebrated with picnics, walking tours and haiku events.

events.name: Celebration of Light
events.description: Three nights of international fireworks competitions light up English Bay in late July and early August, drawing huge beach crowds.

events.name: Vancouver Pride
events.description: One of Canada's biggest Pride celebrations, with a colorful parade through the West End and a festival at Sunset Beach.

attractions.name: Stanley Park
attractions.description: A thousand acres of towering cedars and firs wrapped by the seawall, with totem poles at Brockton Point, secluded beaches and lagoons full of herons. Circle it by bike for postcard views of the Lions Gate Bridge and the North Shore mountains.
attractions.bookingTip: Rent a bike on Denman Street and set off by 9 a.m. to have the seawall mostly to yourself.

attractions.name: Granville Island
attractions.description: A former industrial sandbar beneath the Granville Street Bridge, now home to a bustling public market, artisan studios, a sake brewery and theaters. Graze on smoked salmon, fresh doughnuts and berries, then hop a tiny rainbow-colored ferry across False Creek.
attractions.bookingTip: Arrive before 10 a.m. to beat the crowds and the parking crush, or come by one of the little False Creek ferries.

attractions.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
attractions.description: A swaying 140-meter footbridge strung 70 meters above the Capilano River, with treetop walkways linking giant Douglas firs and a cantilevered cliff walk bolted to the granite canyon wall. It's pricey, but the scale of the rainforest is unforgettable.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy tickets online and ride the free shuttle from Canada Place; go at opening or in the last two hours for thinner crowds.

attractions.name: Gastown
attractions.description: Vancouver's oldest quarter, where cobbled Water Street is lined with Victorian brick warehouses turned boutiques, cocktail bars and chef-driven restaurants. The famous steam clock whistles every 15 minutes to a crowd of raised phones.
attractions.bookingTip: Come for dinner and drinks rather than daytime souvenir shopping, and don't wander east along Hastings Street late at night.

attractions.name: Museum of Anthropology at UBC
attractions.description: Arthur Erickson's soaring glass-and-concrete Great Hall frames monumental totem poles and house posts against sea and mountains, while Bill Reid's cedar sculpture of the Raven and the First Men glows in its rotunda. It's one of the world's great collections of Northwest Coast Indigenous art.
attractions.hours: 10:00–17:00 daily, to 21:00 Thu (closed Mon in winter)
attractions.bookingTip: Visit on a Thursday evening for reduced admission, and pair it with the cliffside trails around the UBC campus.

attractions.name: Grouse Mountain
attractions.description: The Skyride gondola lifts you over 1,100 meters for a panorama of city, harbor and islands, where you can meet rescued grizzly bears, watch lumberjack shows or ski under floodlights in winter. Fit locals skip the gondola and climb the brutally steep Grouse Grind trail instead.
attractions.bookingTip: Book online for a small discount and stay for sunset, when the city lights switch on below.

attractions.name: Vancouver Aquarium
attractions.description: Tucked inside Stanley Park, one of Canada's largest aquariums showcases playful sea otters, sea lions, pulsing jellyfish and a steamy Amazon gallery with sloths. Its marine mammal rescue work makes it more than just a family day out.
attractions.bookingTip: Book timed tickets online and aim for a weekday afternoon, after school groups have left.

attractions.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
attractions.wiki: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
attractions.description: Built by master craftsmen from Suzhou using traditional techniques, this Ming-style scholar's garden is a tranquil world of jade-green ponds, craggy limestone and latticed windows. A free public park next door mirrors its design.
attractions.bookingTip: Join the guided tour included with admission to learn the symbolism behind every rock, plant and window.

attractions.name: Kitsilano Beach
attractions.description: A sandy crescent with volleyball courts, a heated saltwater pool longer than a football field and a skyline view across the water. On sunny days the whole city seems to arrive with frisbees, picnics and paddleboards.
attractions.bookingTip: Stay for sunset, and swim in Kits Pool in summer if the ocean feels too bracing.

attractions.name: Vancouver Art Gallery
attractions.description: Housed in a neoclassical former courthouse downtown, the gallery holds the largest collection of work by Emily Carr, whose swirling forests and totem paintings capture the spirit of the West Coast. Its steps on Robson Street are the city's favorite meeting spot.
attractions.hours: 10:00–17:00 daily (late opening one evening a week)
attractions.bookingTip: Check for the weekly by-donation evening and arrive early, as the line forms well before opening.

hotels.name: Harbourlight Cedar Hotel
hotels.description: A glassy waterfront tower where suites of cedar and slate look over floatplanes landing in Coal Harbour and the forest of Stanley Park beyond. The spa's rainforest-inspired treatments and heated outdoor pool are made for rainy days.

hotels.name: Maple & Mortar Hotel
hotels.description: A red-brick 1890s warehouse on a cobbled Gastown lane, reborn with exposed beams, local Indigenous art and beds made by a Vancouver woodworker. The basement speakeasy mixes cocktails with foraged West Coast botanicals.

hotels.name: Kits Beach Bunkhouse
hotels.description: A cheerful wooden character house a block from the sand, with bright dorms, a big shared kitchen and free loaner bikes and paddleboards in summer. Evening bonfire meetups make it easy to find hiking buddies.

hotels.name: Driftwood & Glass Hotel
hotels.description: Sculptural driftwood, blown-glass lighting and floor-to-ceiling windows define this waterfront hotel facing the Granville Island market across False Creek. Rooms have soaking tubs with views of the marina and mountains.

hotels.name: Yaletown Brick Lofts
hotels.description: Spacious loft apartments in a converted rail warehouse, with full kitchens, in-suite laundry and high timber ceilings. The SkyTrain, seawall and downtown galleries are all within a few minutes' walk.

hotels.name: Pender Lantern House
hotels.nearAttraction: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
hotels.description: A restored 1910s Chinatown society building with recessed balconies, carved teak screens and a rooftop terrace strung with lanterns. The staff run morning walks to the neighborhood's bakeries and herbalists.

restaurants.name: Pender Street Bao Bakery
restaurants.nearAttraction: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
restaurants.description: Trays of glossy barbecue-pork buns, flaky egg tarts and pineapple buns emerge from the ovens all morning at this bustling counter. Grab a paper bag of treats and a milk tea for a picnic in the park by the garden.
restaurants.signatureDish: Baked barbecue-pork bun and warm egg tart

restaurants.name: Yew Street Taquería
restaurants.description: A walk-up window a few blocks from the sand, serving crispy battered-lingcod tacos, carnitas and tangy horchata to salty-haired beachgoers. Take your order down to the logs on the beach for sunset.
restaurants.signatureDish: Beer-battered lingcod tacos with chipotle crema

restaurants.name: Seagull & Sourdough
restaurants.description: A bright waterside café baking naturally leavened loaves and cardamom buns at dawn, with smoked-salmon eggs Benedict for a proper West Coast breakfast. Watch the little ferries dart across False Creek from the window bar.
restaurants.signatureDish: Smoked salmon eggs Benedict on sourdough

restaurants.name: Wildfern Tasting Room
restaurants.description: A cedar-lined dining room overlooking the harbor, where a seasonal tasting menu celebrates wild salmon, foraged mushrooms, sea vegetables and island-grown produce. Pairings come from Okanagan and Vancouver Island wineries.
restaurants.signatureDish: Cedar-smoked wild sockeye with sea asparagus

restaurants.name: Tideline Oyster Bar
restaurants.description: A long marble bar under exposed brick, shucking a dozen varieties of British Columbia oysters alongside spot prawns in season and a smoky seafood chowder. The happy-hour oyster deal packs the place from 3 p.m.
restaurants.signatureDish: BC oysters with mignonette and seafood chowder

restaurants.name: Izakaya Umikaze
restaurants.description: Staff shout a welcome as you enter this lively Robson Street izakaya, where small plates of torched salmon, karaage and udon carbonara fly out of the kitchen. It's loud, fun and perfect for sharing plates late into the night.
restaurants.signatureDish: Torched salmon nigiri and karaage chicken

restaurants.name: Seven Treasures Dim Sum Hall
restaurants.nearAttraction: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
restaurants.description: A chandeliered banquet hall where families gather for weekend dim sum, ticking off shrimp dumplings, rice rolls and custard buns on paper order sheets. Arrive before 10:30 a.m. on weekends to skip the queue.
restaurants.signatureDish: Har gow shrimp dumplings and cheung fun rice rolls

restaurants.name: Capilano Canyon Lodge
restaurants.description: A log-beamed roadhouse with a stone fireplace, local craft beer on tap and hearty plates of salmon burgers, bison chili and wild berry crumble. It's the ideal warm-up after a rainy morning in the canyon.
restaurants.signatureDish: Wild salmon burger with dill slaw

experiences.name: False Creek Sunset Kayak
experiences.description: Paddle out from Granville Island past houseboats and marinas into English Bay as the sun sinks behind the islands and the skyline starts to glow. Harbor seals and herons are frequent company, and no experience is needed.

experiences.name: Coast Mountains Floatplane Flight
experiences.description: Take off from the water in Coal Harbour for a low-level flight over Stanley Park, the Lions Gate Bridge and the glacier-streaked peaks of the Coast Mountains. The pilot narrates the geography as the city shrinks to a toy model below.

experiences.name: Gastown & Chinatown Tasting Walk
experiences.description: Wander from Gastown's cobblestones into historic Chinatown with a local food writer, tasting smoked salmon, bannock-style fry bread, barbecue pork and a craft cocktail. Along the way you'll hear how Indigenous, Chinese and European stories shaped the city.

experiences.name: Rainforest Bathing & Cedar Tea Walk
experiences.description: Slow down on a guided sensory walk through the moss-draped old-growth trails of the Capilano River canyon, with breathing pauses beside rushing water. It ends with a warming cedar-tip tea served in a quiet grove.
